mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes CLK 230/320 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor or CLK 320 replacement engine typically costs between £900 for a used unit and £2,500 for a fully rebuilt engine. Specialist fitting adds £400-£700. Used M111/M112 engines: £900-£1,800 depending on mileage and condition. Reconditioned units: £1,200-£2,200 supply only. Rebuilt units: £1,500-£2,500 with 12-month warranty. Specialist fitting adds £400-£700; dealer labour is significantly higher. 12-month warranty included on all rebuilt units through EnginesMarket.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor or CLK 320 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M111 and M112 are two of Mercedes' most reliable engines from this era. The M112 V6 is particularly bulletproof, with no balance shaft issues (unlike the later M272). The M111 is also robust but suffers from timing chain rattle and supercharger clutch wear. M112 V6: widely regarded as one of Mercedes' most robust modern engines. M111 four-cylinder: timing chain rattle on startup is the main warning sign. Both engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles with proper maintenance. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What is the timing chain rattle on the Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M111 engine can develop a rattling noise on startup due to a worn timing chain tensioner or stretched chain. The camshaft adjuster can also fail, producing a clicking or rattling noise. Rattling on cold start is the classic warning sign. Incorrect engine oil grade can accelerate chain wear. Chain and tensioner replacement costs £800-£1,300 at a specialist. Catch it early - a jumped chain can destroy the engine.

mainEntity.name: What causes loss of power on the Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Loss of power on the CLK 230 Kompressor is often due to supercharger clutch failure, split vacuum pipes, or a faulty recirculating air flap. Supercharger magnetic clutch wear causes loss of boost. Split piping is a common and cheap fix. Fault codes P1525 and P0443 can indicate supercharger issues. Supercharger clutch replacement costs £250-£500 at a specialist.

mainEntity.name: What is the crankshaft position sensor problem on the Mercedes CLK 320?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M112 V6 engine is known for crankshaft position sensor failure, which causes the engine to stall when hot and take 5-15 minutes to restart. The sensor can fail due to heat cycling, with internal wiring breaking. Stalling when hot is the classic symptom. No fault codes are often stored. The sensor is located at the back of the engine and is tricky to access. Specialist replacement costs £150-£300.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes CLK 230/320 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On a CLK 230/320 worth £2,000-£6,000, specialist engine replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is worthwhile if the body and interior are in excellent condition. However, if the car has rust, electrical issues, or poor bodywork, consider scrapping it. CLK values have stabilised at "rock bottom" prices. A clean, well-maintained CLK is worth saving. Rebuilt M111/M112 engines cost £1,500-£2,500 supply only. If the car has other major issues, replacement may not be cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor vs CLK 320 - which engine is more reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are reliable, but the M112 V6 in the CLK 320 is widely considered the more robust engine. It has no balance shaft issues (unlike the later M272) and is known for exceptional longevity. The M111 four-cylinder is also reliable but has more age-related issues. M112 V6 (CLK 320): bulletproof, no major known weaknesses. M111 four-cylinder (CLK 230): timing chain and supercharger clutch are common wear items. Both engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles with proper maintenance. The M112 is generally the more desirable engine for reliability.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLK 230/320 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor and CLK 320 were the performance pillars of the first-generation C208 CLK range from 1997 to 2002. The CLK 230 Kompressor delivered 193 hp via a supercharged 2.3-litre four-cylinder M111 engine, while the CLK 320 offered a silky-smooth 218 hp from its 3.2-litre M112 V6. Both engines were available in coupé (C208) and cabriolet (A208) body styles.

milestones.description: CLK 230 Kompressor launched with M111.973 2.3L supercharged four-cylinder, 193 hp, 280 Nm torque
CLK 320 launched with M112.940 3.2L naturally aspirated V6, 218 hp, 308 Nm torque
Cabriolet (A208) variants introduced for both CLK 230 and CLK 320
Facelift: CLK 230 Kompressor upgraded to M111.975 with 197 hp
C208 production ends; CLK 230 and CLK 320 replaced by C209 generation engines

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every petrol engine fitted to the Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor and CLK 320 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLK 230/320 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor and CLK 320 are powered by two of Mercedes' most respected engines of the era - the supercharged M111 four-cylinder and the naturally aspirated M112 V6. Both are generally robust and reliable when properly maintained. However, age-related issues do arise: the M111 suffers from timing chain rattle and supercharger clutch wear, while the M112 is known for crankshaft position sensor failure and oil consumption from worn valve stem seals. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Rattle - The M111 Kompressor's Most Common Warning Sign
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to slacken and produce a rattling noise on startup. Incorrect engine oil grade can accelerate chain wear. The camshaft adjuster can also fail, producing a clicking or rattling noise.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if timing chain itself hasn't stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
Supply & fit fully rebuilt M111 engine with new timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped and valves have contacted pistons

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start is the early warning sign. Don't ignore it - specialist timing chain replacement at £800-£1,300 resolves the issue if done promptly. The M111 is otherwise a robust engine, and replacing the timing chain before failure can extend engine life significantly. If the chain has already slipped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M111 Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor engine prices

problems.h4: Supercharger Clutch Failure - Loss of Boost on the CLK 230 Kompressor
problems.rootCause: The supercharger (Kompressor) magnetic clutch bearing wears out, producing a squealing or rattling noise. The clutch can also fail electrically due to corroded contacts or a faulty relay. Symptoms include loss of power, whistling or squealing noises on acceleration, and fault codes P1525 or P0443.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if clutch is the only failed component

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Specialist rebuild of kompressor unit with new bearings, seals, and clutch service
Complete replacement engine with serviced supercharger, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best when engine has other issues or supercharger failure has caused internal damage

problems.recommendation: The M111 Kompressor engine is otherwise robust. On a CLK 230 with a failed supercharger but otherwise healthy engine, specialist clutch replacement for £250-£500 or a full supercharger rebuild for £500-£900 is the right answer - far more cost-effective than replacing the whole engine. However, if the supercharger has failed catastrophically and sent debris into the engine, a replacement engine may be required.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M111 supercharger repair for your Mercedes CLK 230 Kompressor

problems.h4: Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure - The M112 V6's Most Common Electrical Fault
problems.rootCause: The crankshaft position sensor fails due to heat cycling, causing internal wiring to break. Symptoms include the engine stalling when hot, difficulty restarting after 5-15 minutes, and no fault codes stored. The sensor is located at the back of the engine and is tricky to access.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect wiring harness, camshaft sensors, and ECU connections
repairOptions.longevity: Required if CPS replacement doesn't resolve the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt M112 engine with new sensors and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if crankshaft sensor failure has caused catastrophic engine damage

problems.recommendation: The M112 V6 is widely regarded as one of Mercedes' most reliable engines. Crankshaft position sensor failure is the most common issue and is easily fixed. If your CLK 320 stalls when hot and won't restart for 5-15 minutes, start with the CPS - it's a £150-£300 specialist fix. The M112 engine is otherwise robust and, with proper maintenance, can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M112 Mercedes CLK 320 engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - Worn Valve Stem Seals on the M112 V6
problems.rootCause: Over time, valve stem seals harden and crack, allowing oil to seep past the valve guides and into the combustion chambers, where it is burned. Symptoms include blue smoke on startup, increased oil consumption, and in severe cases, fouled spark plugs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals (cylinder head remains on engine)
Supply & fit fully rebuilt M112 engine with new seals, bearings, and timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 150k+ miles or when oil consumption exceeds 1L/1,000 miles

problems.recommendation: Oil consumption on the M112 is typically due to worn valve stem seals - not piston rings. If you're burning oil but the engine runs smoothly, specialist valve stem seal replacement at £1,000-£1,800 resolves the issue. The M112 is otherwise bulletproof, so it's worth fixing rather than replacing the entire engine.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for M112 valve stem seal repair for your Mercedes CLK 320
